facts.big: If I had more money, I’d buy it
facts.label: Falar de compras e sonhos
facts.sub: Use if + passado e would + verbo base: If I had more money, I’d buy it. Para conselho, use If I were you, I’d…

facts.label: Se + passado, would + base
facts.sub: Use if + passado para o sonho e would + verbo base para o resultado: If I had more money, I’d buy it. É uma situação hipotética: eu não tenho dinheiro agora.

facts.label: Se eu fosse você
facts.sub: Use If I were you, I’d… para dar conselho. Com I, he e she, prefira were: If I were you, I’d ask. Isso soa natural e educado em muitas conversas.

compare.ask: If I had more money, I’d buy it.
compare.br: No Brasil, dizemos “se eu tivesse dinheiro, eu compraria”.

compare.us: Em inglês, use if + passado e I’d + verbo base: If I had more money, I’d buy it. Com I, he e she, use were em conselhos: If I were you, I’d wait.

solo: Peça uma experiência pessoal do aluno com essa diferença.
group: Leia as duas colunas e peça que apontem a maior diferença.

extra90: Peça que cada aluno invente uma pergunta igual para o colega.
answers: If I had… talks about a dream or unlikely situation. → Verdadeiro (Yes.)
After if we use the past: If I had money. → Verdadeiro (Yes.)
We say “If I would have money.” → Falso (We say If I had money.)

pages.title: A bike shop in Portland · 1/3
paragraphs: It is a rainy morning in Portland. Tom stops in front of a bike shop. There is a silver bike in the window. He wonders if he can afford it. Bea works at the shop and loves bikes. She walks out to talk to him.

“That is a beautiful bike. Do you want to try it, Tom?” says Bea. “I’d love to, but it’s too expensive. If I had more money, I’d buy it.” says Tom. “If I were you, I’d ask about our payment plan.” says Bea.
